repository.name: awesome-battery-data
repository.title: Battery Data Discovery Lab
repository.description: Find traceable battery datasets and compare how temperature, cycling conditions and holdout choices shape capacity fade.
repository.summary: A forked directory of electrochemical, microstructural, safety, modeling, and analysis resources. Synthetic fade scenarios explain why protocol metadata matters before combining datasets.
repository.audience: Battery researchers, students, and data practitioners choosing data for a specific question.

model.equation: k = (f/100000) · exp((T−25)/20) · √C-rate; retention = 100 exp(−kt); capacity = Q₀ exp(−kt).
assumptions: A transparent exponential fade curve is an educational proxy, not a fitted lifetime prediction.
Temperature and C-rate remain constant for every cycle.
Throughput integrates remaining capacity at an illustrative 3.7 V cell voltage; calendar aging is omitted.
Paul Gasper and upstream contributors retain attribution for the resource directory.
The source list spans chemistries, formats, protocols, measurements, and separate licenses; a link is not a quality guarantee.
The displayed exponential relation and coupled stress factors are teaching assumptions, not measurements from any listed cell.
model.introduction: No linked dataset is downloaded or fitted here. The same invented fade equation is used to reveal how temperature, rate, and normalization can confound a cross-study comparison.

modules.title: Choose data for the question
modules.objective: Match the desired battery claim to the measurements and provenance a dataset must contain.
steps: Open the electrochemical-data table and identify its chemistry, cell format, study, and measurement columns.
Apply a 25°C, 1C synthetic protocol and read normalized retention at 1,000 cycles.
Name one question that charge/discharge data can support and one that requires EIS or imaging.
modules.reflection: Which source fields would you record before treating a dataset as evidence for cycle aging?

modules.title: Expose a temperature confound
modules.objective: Hold the synthetic cell fixed while changing only temperature.
steps: Keep the fade coefficient, capacity, and C-rate from the baseline.
Change temperature to 45°C, predict the direction of retention change, and run.
Return to the directory and ask whether the two real studies you might compare report matching temperatures.

checkpoints.label: Retention falls below 70% in this toy case

modules.reflection: Why would fitting one pooled curve across different test temperatures conceal a study-design difference?

modules.title: Separate normalization from cell size
modules.objective: Explain why absolute capacity and normalized retention answer different questions.
steps: Restore 25°C and 1C, then change initial capacity from 100 Ah to 50 Ah.
Predict which metric stays unchanged and which scales by one half.
Use the cell-format and chemistry columns to explain why normalization alone does not make datasets interchangeable.

checkpoints.label: The smaller cell retains its own Ah scale

modules.reflection: What additional metadata would you need to compare a pouch-cell result with a cylindrical-cell result?

modules.title: Create a reproducible dataset shortlist
modules.objective: State selection criteria and limitations before any download or model fitting.
steps: Apply a gentler 0.5C protocol at 25°C and inspect retention and throughput.
Choose a candidate from the directory and record its citation, download location, test conditions, and reuse terms.
Export the synthetic scenario as an assumptions example, clearly separated from the selected dataset.

checkpoints.label: Low-rate retention at the fixed horizon

modules.reflection: Write the inclusion/exclusion criteria and the missing-data questions that must be resolved before training a model.
